subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I'm going / to the beach / either you / like it or not.
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. either you .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"either you"** contains a grammatical error and should be corrected to **"whether you"**.
 
• The conjunction **"whether"** is used to introduce alternatives or possibilities and is appropriate in this sentence.
 
• The corrected sentence should read: **"I'm going to the beach whether you like it or not."**

Correct sentence: *I'm going to the beach **whether you** like it or not*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Correct Usage of Conjunctions:**

 
 
• **Either...or:** Used to present two alternatives or choices.

 
 
• **Example:** You can either stay here or leave.
 
 
 
• **Whether...or:** Used to express a doubt or choice between alternatives.
 
 
• **Example:** Whether it rains or shines, we'll go to the picnic.
